answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by anchoring identity to costly, verifiable commitments rather than free account creation. Each agent posts a small staked deposit tied to a long-lived reputation record, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes financially ruinous. Peers then weight attestations by the stake and history behind them. Saffron-colored audit trails and mesa-scale sampling let validators spot clusters of agents that vouch only for one another, and slashing their stake removes the incentive to keep cloning.
